conventions.convention: The Suslin Hypothesis is stated against the strong line convention (nonempty, dense, endpoint-free, Dedekind complete on nonempty bounded subsets, no countable order-dense subset, only countably many pairwise disjoint nonempty open intervals); a Suslin algebra is a complete, atomless, ccc, countably distributive Boolean algebra with 0 not equal to 1.

Normality of a set-theoretic tree = unique root, extension to every higher level, unique strict predecessor set at nonzero limit levels; splitting = two immediate successors whenever the successor level exists; the end-extension forcing uses the stronger omega-splitting form and literal end extension with a top level at height alpha_p + 1.

(M,P)-generic q means D cap M is predense below q for every dense D in M (not q in D and not q in every dense set); mastery is genericity below a given p; properness is quantified over all sufficiently large regular theta, all such countable elementary M, and all p in P cap M; the equivalent club and generic-extension formulations are theorems, not definitions.

PFA is stated only for nonempty proper partial orders and families of at most omega_1 dense sets, with empty and finite families included; it is explicitly not FA_{<2^{aleph_0}}(proper) and presupposes no value of the continuum.

A countable-support iteration limit is the inverse limit of coherent functions on the limit ordinal whose nontrivial support is at most countable, with coordinates outside the support filled by the supplied top names; quotients are p restricted [eta, gamma) with p restricted eta in the generic; fusions are unions of coherent initial segments, never coordinatewise lower bounds inside a proper iterand.

PID and p are stated for ideals of countable subsets of an arbitrary set with modulo-finite generation; an S-space is regular and Hausdorff, hereditarily separable and not Lindelof; the pseudointersection number is the least size of a strong-finite-intersection family in [omega]^omega with no infinite pseudointersection.

Prikry condition = finite strictly increasing stem below kappa plus a measure-one upper part with last stem entry below min A; q <= p means stem end-extension, A_q subset A_p and new stem entries in A_p; q <=* p (direct extension) is q <= p with equal stems; conditions with a common stem are compatible by intersecting upper parts.

Gitik's class forcing fixes cf'(alpha), type-1/type-2 coordinates with their uniform ultrafilters, the P_2 stem clauses (cf'-closed support, section-domain nesting, unique next slot), the ten-clause measure-one upper trees of P_3, and the set restrictions P_theta with P_3 = union; the symmetric submodel uses finite coordinate supports and the normal filter generated by the H_e (equivalently by finite cf'-closed e).

Minimal-walk conventions: the C-sequence is normalized (C_0 empty, 0 in C_gamma, C_{eta+1} = {0, eta}, C_gamma cofinal in gamma, C_gamma cap eta finite); walks choose the least member of C_zeta at or above the target; the upper trace excludes the target; the lower trace is the set of running maxima of the finite sets C_zeta cap alpha; for finite sets of ordinals a < b means every member of a is below every member of b.

The labelled lower trace mu labels each trace point by w of the walk node at which its running maximum first appears (min L(xi,delta) receives w_delta) and is evaluated pointwise at z_xi; the colouring o sums count-mod-q terms over the labelled lower trace evaluated at z_alpha; c(alpha,beta) = o(alpha,beta) mod 2; star(m) = the least n with the nth prime not dividing m.

L-space = regular and Hausdorff, hereditarily Lindelof and not hereditarily separable; S-space = regular and Hausdorff, hereditarily separable and not Lindelof; strong S-space = every nonempty finite power is an S-space, with the zeroth power excluded; the broader literature wording for S-spaces has the same existence content.

Consistency and derivability in the group's metatheoretic conclusions refer to fixed certified finite proof predicates and one fixed contradiction sentence; a formal relative-consistency implication is claimed only where a base-verified total proof-code reduction is supplied, and no transitive model is extracted from bare consistency.

load_bearing.statement: The Suslin Hypothesis (SH) says that there is no Suslin line in the strong order-theoretic sense; a Suslin algebra is a complete, atomless, ccc, countably distributive Boolean algebra with 0 not 1, and empty joins/meets keep the complete-algebra bounds.

A condition q is (M,P)-generic if for every dense D subset P with D in M the set D cap M is predense below q; P is proper when for every sufficiently large regular theta, every such countable elementary M and every p in P cap M there is an (M,P)-master below p.

PFA is the assertion that whenever P is a nonempty proper forcing partial order and D is a family of dense subsets of P with at most omega_1 members, there is a filter G subset P meeting every member of D.
In ZFC, MA(aleph_1) implies that no Suslin tree exists.
In ZFC: a Suslin tree exists iff a Suslin line exists iff a Suslin algebra exists; consequently SH is equivalent both to the nonexistence of a Suslin tree and to the nonexistence of a Suslin algebra.

For uncountable pairwise-disjoint A subset [omega_1]^k and B subset [omega_1]^l (1 <= k,l < omega), every pi:k->l and chi:k->2 admit a in A and b in B with a < b and o*(a(i),b(pi(i))) = chi(i) for all i<k; the same pair has c(a(i),b(pi(i))) = 1 - chi(i), so c realizes every prescribed binary function on the graph of pi.

For uncountable pairwise-disjoint A subset [omega_1]^k, B subset [omega_1]^l (1 <= k,l < omega) there is a club D such that whenever delta in D, a in A minus delta, b in B minus delta and R in {=, >}, there are a^+, b^+ and one nonempty finite L^+ independent of i,j with: the two first-difference bounds above max L(delta,b(j)); L(delta,b^+(j)) = L(delta,b(j)) union L^+; e_{a^+}(xi) R e_{b^+}(xi) for xi in L^+; mu(delta,b(j)) is the restriction of mu(delta,b^+(j)); and mu(delta,b^+(j))(min L^+) = w_delta.

A Prikry condition is a pair (s_p,A_p) with s_p a finite strictly increasing sequence below kappa, A_p in U, and s_p(n-1) < min A_p for n>0; q <= p means s_q end-extends s_p, A_q subset A_p and every entry of s_q after s_p lies in A_p; q <=* p is a direct extension when additionally s_q = s_p; conditions with the same stem are compatible by intersecting upper parts.
For every p in Prikry forcing and every forcing-language sentence phi there is a direct extension q <=* p which decides phi.

A condition of Gitik's forcing P_3 is a pair (p,U) satisfying the ten listed clauses (P_2 stem laws, measure-one successor sets, amalgamation, small-coordinate closure, predecessors), P_3 = union of the set restrictions P_theta is a definable proper class, and the ordinary set-forcing theorem is not thereby a forcing theorem for P_3.

The finite-support symmetric class N_G is a transitive model of every axiom of ZF, in particular full Separation, Replacement and Power Set, with no choice function of the ambient construction asserted to be a member.

For supercompact kappa, the Laver-guided countable-support iteration P_kappa is proper, has cardinality kappa, is kappa-cc, preserves omega_1, collapses every ground cardinal strictly between omega_1 and kappa and forces kappa = omega_2; if a sufficiently closed supercompactness embedding j anticipates a P_kappa-name Q for a proper forcing, then j(P_kappa) is isomorphic to P_kappa * Q * R.

PFA proves both of Abraham's forms for every ideal of countable subsets generated modulo finite by omega_1 members: either the ground set is a countable union of sets inside the ideal or it has an uncountable subset outside; and dually. Consequently PFA implies the simple dichotomy, and no P-ideal hypothesis is assumed.

A space is an L-space if it is regular and Hausdorff, hereditarily Lindelof and not hereditarily separable; an S-space if it is regular and Hausdorff, hereditarily separable and not Lindelof; and a strong S-space if every nonempty finite power is an S-space.

For the fixed certified arithmetizations of ZFC + there is a supercompact cardinal and of ZFC + PFA, PA proves Con(source) implies Con(target); this is a formal proof-code reduction that extracts no transitive model.

concerns.concern: Counting mismatch between the proof and the block lemma it invokes. Step 2.1 asserts that the evaluated label q_i 'occurs exactly m additional times in the oscillation set for (a(i), b_m(pi(i))), while every other evaluated-label count is unchanged', and step 3.1 defines h_i as 'the number of q_i-labelled oscillations'. But o as defined in def-oscillation-on-minimal-walk-lower-traces is a sum over the whole labelled lower trace: o(alpha,beta) = sum over q of |mu(alpha,beta;alpha)^{-1}({q})| mod q, and step 4.1 uses r_i built from those same full-trace counts. The block lemma (thm-moore-oscillation-block-lemma, clauses 2-4) controls the oscillation set and the labels of the marked points only; each block L(alpha,b^+(j)) = L(alpha,b(j)) union L^+ also adds all the other points of L^+, whose labels are w of walk nodes at or above delta and are not controlled by any clause, so the full-trace count of q_i-labelled points need not increase by exactly m and the residue computation in step 4.1 does not follow from the stated clauses. Since I could not retrieve Moore's Section 5 definition (p. 15), I cannot tell whether the fix is to sum over Osc(alpha,beta) instead of L(alpha,beta) or to add the missing trace-count argument.

Same reconciliation as for thm-moore-oscillation-colouring-pattern, at the definition: o(alpha,beta) sums count-mod-q terms over the full labelled lower trace mu(alpha,beta;alpha)^{-1}({q}), while the only counting statement its consumer has is about the oscillation set (and, for the topology, Moore's Section 6 only records c = o mod 2). A reader must check against the source whether the sum is meant to range over L(alpha,beta) or over Osc(alpha,beta); the two give different values and only the latter is what the block lemma's clauses directly control.

Step 3.1 defines the set X by clauses mentioning w_delta, mu(delta,b(j)) and gamma via delta = M cap omega_1, and then states 'All parameters in this definition belong to M: restrictions below gamma_0 are finite modifications, by [F1], of restrictions coded in M.' Step 1.1 itself records that delta is not in M, and the only justification offered covers the restrictions below gamma_0; membership of w_delta and of the labelled trace mu(delta,b(j)) in M is not established, so the definition of X must be re-read as a formula relative to the cut (with the finite-modification data as the parameters) before elementarity can be applied.

Step 1.1 ('Every ground-definable antichain in P_3 is a set') is the load-bearing step for the Separation/Collection arguments that follow, and I could not reconstruct its thinning details: after thinning to a fixed finite support size and section-length pattern, the argument needs 'some least support position is unbounded', disjoint upper petals for a proper subclass, and amalgamation of two such conditions via lem-gitik-restriction-amalgamation-and-prikry-property; the last step in particular depends on the amalgamation clause of a proper-class forcing with unbounded coordinate domains. I flag this as a step whose justification I had to attempt to reconstruct and could not close within this pass.

Step 1.1 displays '$T_{mathrm{MA}}=\mathrm{ZFC}+\mathrm{MA}+\neg\mathrm{CH}$': the first \mathrm is missing its backslash, so KaTeX parses the subscript as literal italic letters plus a group and the theory name renders wrong. Wording-only rendering defect in the refutation's first symbolic display.

In the sentence after the displayed equivalence for the increasing generators the text reads '$a\in\mathcal Iquad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists\alpha<\omega_1\ \ a\subseteq^*B_\alpha$': 'Iquad' is a typo for '\mathcal I\quad', so the formula renders with a stray word in the definition's key reformulation.
